correctness.rationale: For N>=2 at least one positive real zero, boundary speed is an even strictly decreasing sum of Poisson kernels on (0,pi). The inverse-phase derivative h is even and strictly increasing in circular distance. Its 2pi interval mass J(c) has derivative h(c+pi)-h(c-pi)>0 for 0<c<Npi, including the wraparound case. Fiber interval centers are phi+(2k+1)pi, so nearest and farthest centers give both exact profiles; strict monotonicity makes the phases unique and yields the parity rule. Evaluating J at the two optimal centers gives exact gaps; Taylor expansion yields strictly positive cusp coefficients. Standard-library checker replay passed 7208 finite diagnostics across 34 zero arrays; universal validity comes from the analytic proof, not numerical samples.

value.rationale: The exact min/max angular-gap profiles solve two canonical, competing physical packing and covering objectives for every aligned finite Blaschke circle covering; optimizing target phase is a genuine design decision. Sharp uniqueness, parity-dependent compatibility, and nonzero phase-error cusps make a complete structural classification, not a numerical example or mere restatement of a Poisson formula. The minimal-atom optimal prediction design interpretation supplies a natural concrete use for these specific invariants.
